page.overview:
Who is Keeper of Dreams?

The Keeper of Dreams is a fictional monster created by Gary Myers for his Dreamlands short story "Passing of a Dreamer".

The Keeper of Dreams is a living creature disguised as an idol that squats on an altar made "of what the unimaginative think are merely human bones", behind a secret door in a hidden alley in the dream town of Ulthar. Its appearance is similar to a salamander with "improperly placed" eyes, flabby claws and "fretted wings". Whatever it has "in lieu of a mouth" made ex-priest Snireth-Ko scream when he saw it.

The Keeper of Dreams is known for its ability to grant wishes, or more accurately sell them. What it demands as payment for its clients' desires is unknown, but ominous, apparently involving the death of the client, whose bones are afterwards added to the Keeper's altar. The fees are kept in a mysterious painted box, so the Keeper may someday use them when the Old Gods awaken to reclaim the Earth, either as a form of blackmail or "to purchase unspeakable favours" from them. (: "Passing of a Dreamer")

In the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu, the Keeper's is payment is revealed to be its clients' souls, kept in silvery globes inside the box. (: H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands) Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Other Supernatural Beings Category:Extra-Dimensional Characters
